_comment: U1–U8 teaching units. Source of truth: curriculum.md section 5. Units are the ORDER WE TEACH; modules are the order NetAcad numbers them. They deliberately disagree.

u1.title: Packet Tracer Boot Camp
u1.why: Competitors lose points to the tool, not the networking. They can't find a device, cable the wrong port, or forget to save.
u1.gate: Given a written topology, build and cable it correctly in under 5 minutes with all links up.
u1.netacad: Modules 1–2 plus the introductory Packet Tracer activities.

u2.title: Ethernet & Switching Foundations
u2.why: Round 1's quiz is drawn from Modules 3–7. This unit IS Round 1.
u2.gate: In Simulation mode, step one PDU end to end and correctly name the layer at which each header is added and removed, without notes, then predict a switch's forward/flood/filter decision from a given MAC table.

u3.title: IP Addressing
u3.why: Everything after this point assumes a student can look at an address and a mask and know what network it is on.
u3.gate: 10 conversions plus 8 same-subnet determinations, all correct, in under 6 minutes, no calculator, then configure DHCP for a LAN and prove a client lease.

u4.title: Switching & Layer 3 Forwarding
u4.why: Modules 21 and 22 unlock at Round 2, out of numeric order. They are the deep-dive counterparts to Modules 7 and 8. Teaching them here, before 12–17, is the whole reason this curriculum is organized in units rather than module numbers.
u4.gate: Given a two-router topology and a PDU, correctly name the source and destination MAC and IP addresses at every hop, without notes.

u5.title: Routing Between Networks
u5.why: A router is the boundary. Until a student can explain why PC1 cannot reach PC2 without one, and break it four different ways and fix it, they are guessing.
u5.gate: Given the reference topology with one planted fault (bad gateway, missing route, wrong mask, or shut interface), identify and fix it in under 5 minutes and prove the fix with a ping and a tracert.

u6.title: Services & Troubleshooting
u6.why: This is where the State Round is won. Modules 15–17 turn Packet Tracer from a diagramming tool into a troubleshooting environment.
u6.gate: Given a topology with two planted faults of different types (one addressing, one service), find both using the diagnostic sequence, narrate the reasoning aloud, fix both, and verify, in under 12 minutes.

u7.title: Advanced Networking: Design, Number Systems & Subnetting
u7.why: Subnetting is the single highest-value Semifinals skill. Module 20 supplies the binary and hexadecimal fluency; Module 23 spends it.
u7.gate: Given a /24 and four differently-sized host requirements, produce a complete, non-overlapping subnet plan (network, mask, range, broadcast, gateway) in under 8 minutes, no calculator. Then address a live Packet Tracer topology from that plan and prove full reachability.

u8.title: Capstone Mock Round
u8.why: A full simulated round: 10-question open-internet quiz on a 20-minute budget, then a multi-device lab with planted faults. Every mock round ends with an after-action review naming points lost to knowledge, to speed, and to process.
u8.gate: At least 85% of available lab points inside the time budget, twice in a row on different topologies.
